name: OX Quiz Widget
description: A mobile-friendly educational OX (true/false) quiz widget that shows one question at a time, gives instant feedback with explanations, and tracks progress.

requirement.summary: Build an OX quiz interface for an educational mobile app. The user views questions one at a time, selects O or X, sees whether the answer is correct along with an explanation, tracks progress, and can retake the quiz.
details: Display the OX quiz question list one question at a time
Provide O and X answer buttons for the user to choose from
After selection, show whether the answer is correct and display an explanation for the question
Disable further answer changes for the current question once an answer is selected, and provide a 'Next' action to move to the next question
Display progress as text (e.g., '3/10 completed') alongside a visual progress bar
Show a completion summary (score, number correct/incorrect) when all questions are finished
Provide a 'Retry' feature that resets all state and restarts the quiz from the first question
Responsive design optimized for mobile and tablet viewports
Apply transition animations when moving between questions and when showing answer feedback, using Tailwind transition/animation utilities

Accessibility: support full keyboard navigation (Tab focus, Enter/Space to activate; optional O/X keyboard shortcuts), visible focus rings, ARIA labels on buttons, and aria-live announcements for feedback and progress
Color scheme: green for correct answers, red for incorrect answers, gray for neutral/unanswered states
Use the system default font stack (Tailwind font-sans)

Component structure: QuizContainer (overall quiz layout and state management), QuestionCard (displays the current question), AnswerButtons (O/X selection buttons), ProgressBar (progress display), ResultDisplay (correct/incorrect feedback and explanation)
State management: current question index, user answers, correctness per answer, and quiz completion status
Include built-in sample quiz data (e.g., 10 questions each with question text, correct answer O or X, and explanation) and accept questions via props with typed interfaces
